hedges.reason: This is the closest expression of the hedge thesis: OpenAI does not hold the top text-arena rank with style control off. The primary fails at the low end in two ways: OpenAI ships only a weak or small GPT model, or ships no GPT model at all. In both cases the top slot belongs to a Google or Anthropic model, not an OpenAI one. Taking OpenAI NO covers both Google and Anthropic at once, so I do not have to guess which of them leads.

This covers the high-end failure of NO on C5 and C6. The most plausible route to a debut at 1500 or above, and especially 1520 or above, is a generational OpenAI release that it would brand GPT-6. A public GPT-6 release by year end is the world in which the high rungs pay out.

claims.reason: C1 resolves NO only if the first GPT-named OpenAI model to be listed scores below 1450, or if none is listed by December 31. In either case OpenAI has no new frontier-level text model in 2026. The July 31 top rank would then rest on an older OpenAI model, and as of mid-2026 I do not think that model leads the leaderboard ahead of Gemini or Claude. So OpenAI would not be ranked first.

A debut at 1520 or above would be a first-day jump of roughly 20 or more points over an already crowded frontier. Past incremental GPT-5.x releases have not produced gaps that large. A jump of that size fits a generational model, which OpenAI would release and brand as GPT-6 within the 2026 window.
